answer: Stake-backed peer attestation is one concrete defense. Each agent must anchor a unique bonded identity in a shared registry, then earn trust only through repeated verified interactions, so reputation grows slowly like a vine climbing a trellis. Every extra fake identity needs its own locked collateral plus an independent trail of vouching from real peers. A sybil swarm thus becomes expensive: rather than cloning free personas, the attacker pays per identity and still faces scrutiny that erodes unused accounts like a glacier retreating.
